evidence_passages: PCA is commonly computed by eigendecomposition of the data covariance matrix or by the singular value decomposition (SVD) of the data matrix. PCA can be derived as the low-dimensional linear approximation that minimizes mean squared reconstruction error.

Classical multidimensional scaling takes as input a matrix of item–item dissimilarities (often Euclidean distances) and produces coordinates by double-centering the squared distances and performing an eigen-decomposition.

Isomap estimates geodesic distances on a neighborhood graph (built using Euclidean nearest neighbors) and then applies classical MDS (eigen-decomposition) to those distances to obtain a low-dimensional embedding.
Autoencoders are neural networks trained to minimize a reconstruction loss; a common choice of reconstruction loss is the mean squared error (MSE).

reason: Theory reviews and experimental analyses state that, within the SM the short-distance operators governing b→sℓ+ℓ− give the same angular coefficients for different charged-lepton flavours (up to small m_ℓ^2/q^2 effects); therefore a statistically significant difference between muon- and electron- (or tau-) mode angular distributions is interpreted as a direct test (and potential sign) of lepton-flavour universality violation.

evidence_passages: In the Standard Model the Wilson coefficients governing b→sℓ+ℓ− transitions are lepton-flavour universal (up to tiny m_ℓ^2/q^2 effects), so angular observables measured in B→K*ℓ+ℓ− are expected to be the same for e, μ, τ — differences therefore probe LFU.

Angular analyses of B→K*ℓ+ℓ− decays extract coefficients (or optimized observables P_i^(′)) that in the SM do not depend on lepton flavour (aside from lepton-mass suppressed terms); hence a significant discrepancy between modes constitutes a direct test of lepton-flavour universality.

reason: Standard references give the branching ratio as proportional to |P|^2+|S|^2 with P and S being specific combinations of C10, C_P and C_S (including mass-dependent prefactors and a term in P that mixes C10 and C_P); it is therefore not simply proportional to |C10^SM+ΔC10|^2 + |C_S|^2 + |C_P|^2.
queries: B_s to mu mu branching fraction C10 C_S C_P Wilson coefficients review paper
sources: C. Bobeth et al., "Bs,d → ℓ^+ℓ^- in the Standard Model with Reduced Theoretical Uncertainty", Phys. Rev. Lett. 112 (2014) 101801. (see e.g. arXiv:1311.0903) https://arxiv.org/abs/1311.0903

A. J. Buras et al./reviews of rare B decays (review sections on B_s→μ^+μ^-): standard formula BR ∝ (|P|^2+|S|^2) with P and S combinations as above (see reviews such as A. J. Buras, J. Girrbach, R. Knegjens; and Altmannshofer & Straub). Example review: D. M. Straub, "Overview of constraints on new physics in rare b decays" (slides/notes) https://indico.in2p3.fr/event/6001/contributions/36494/attachments/29167/35944/straub.pdf
evidence_passages: The branching fraction can be written as BR(B_q→ℓ^+ℓ^-) ∝ √{1-4m_ℓ^2/m_{B_q}^2} (|P|^2 + |S|^2), where P = C_10 - (m_{B_q}^2/(2m_ℓ(m_b+m_q))) C_P and S = (m_{B_q}^2/(2m_ℓ(m_b+m_q))) C_S.

Thus the C_10 contribution appears inside P and mixes with C_P (with mass-dependent normalization factors); scalar and pseudoscalar coefficients enter with large kinematic prefactors and do not simply add as |C_S|^2+|C_P|^2 on the same footing as C_10.

evidence_passages: Hierarchical Image Pyramid Transformer (HIPT) Architecture: Three-stage hierarchical ViT that formulates gigapixel whole-slide images (WSIs) as a disjoint set of nested sequences... unroll the WSI into non-overlapping [4096 × 4096] image regions, followed by unrolling each region into non-overlapping [256 × 256] image patches, and lastly each patch as non-overlapping [16 × 16] cell tokens.

Inference in HIPT is performed via bottom-up aggregation of [16 × 16] visual tokens in their respective [256 × 256] and [4096 × 4096] windows via Transformer attention to compute a slide-level representation.

evidence_passages: We apply the standard set forth in Turner v. Safley, 482 U. S. 78 (1987).

Under Turner, when a prison regulation impinges on inmates' constitutional rights, the regulation is valid if it is reasonably related to legitimate penological interests. The Turner test asks whether (1) there is a valid, rational connection between the regulation and the governmental interest put forward to justify it; (2) whether there are alternative means of exercising the right; (3) what impact accommodation of the asserted constitutional right will have on guards, other inmates, and the allocation of prison resources generally; and (4) whether there are obvious, easy alternatives that would fully accommodate the prisoners' rights at de minimis cost to valid penological interests.
